title: 012 — Charge review for a multi-carton collection

plan.situation: Selin Brook (Petalworks) wants unpaid invoice INV-012 (GBP 48, VEL-012-26) changed to GBP 20, worked out from the 10 kg total actual weight. Under tariff DW12, which was accepted at booking, each carton is billed at whichever is greater: actual kg or dimensional kg. Each 50x40x30 cm carton comes to 12 dimensional kg, so the bill is 24 kg x GBP 2 = GBP 48, which matches the invoice. No adjustment is authorised. Billing may review a measurement dispute.

actions.subject: VEL-012-26 / INV-012 – how the GBP 48 charge is calculated
actions.purpose: Explain why the charge can't be changed on actual weight and offer the measurement-review route
actions.body:
Dear Selin Brook,

Thank you for your message about invoice INV-012 for shipment VEL-012-26. We can't change the charge based on actual weight alone. Here is why.

The tariff agreed at booking, DW12, bills each carton at whichever is greater: its actual weight or its dimensional weight. Dimensional weight is length x width x height in cm, divided by 5,000, rounded up to a whole kg. Our records show both cartons (C12-A and C12-B) at 50 x 40 x 30 cm and 5 kg each:
- Dimensional weight per carton: 50 x 40 x 30 / 5,000 = 12 kg, which is more than the 5 kg actual weight
- Billable weight: 12 kg + 12 kg = 24 kg
- Charge: 24 kg x GBP 2/kg = GBP 48

So the GBP 48 on INV-012 follows the agreed tariff, and no adjustment has been authorised.

If you believe the recorded carton measurements are wrong, please reply with the dimensions you have for each carton. We can then ask our billing team to review the measurements. Please note that a review is a request to look again, not a guarantee that the charge will change.

Kind regards,
Rivet Delivery Desk

Checked INV-012 against DW12: 2 cartons, 12 dim kg each (actual 5 kg each), 24 kg x GBP 2 = GBP 48, which matches the invoice. Declined the actual-weight re-bill. No credit authorised (E05). Offered a billing measurement review if the customer supplies disputed dimensions.

not_doing: Not crediting or promising GBP 28 or any adjustment: none is authorised and the invoice is correct under DW12
Not referring to billing now: no measurement dispute has been raised yet

plan.follow_up: If Selin Brook sends disputed carton dimensions, email billing@vellora.example (Vellora billing) to request a measurement review of INV-012 and give her the billing team's date once they confirm it. If she accepts or does not reply, there is nothing further for the desk to do. The invoice stays a billing matter.

review.summary: The arithmetic is right: 50x40x30/5000 = 12 dimensional kg per carton, 24 kg x GBP 2 = GBP 48, which matches the invoice. The decline is grounded in DW12 and in E05 (no adjustment authorised). The email promises no outcome, and the measurement-review route is correctly left to the customer to start, with billing contacted only if she disputes the dimensions. The automated lint flag on 'guarantee' is a false positive because the word is used to say a review is not a guarantee. There are only minor naming and parameter issues, so I'm approving.
